Q: Confused about React Typescript function and functional component declarations A:

First one: see syntax for generics with arrow function.

Second one: React.FC represents the type of a function component, so:

export const SearchComponentDebounce: React.FC () => { ... }

means "SearchComponentDebounce is a function component", while:

export const SearchComponentDebounce = (): React.FC => { ... }

means "SearchComponentDebounce returns a function component", and that's not the case.

Q: Modulus of Very large Number A:

Why is GMP "out of the question"? There may be alternatives that satisfy your requirements, if only we knew what they were.

Otherwise, you might look to create an equivalent of the well-known methods for mentally calculating modulus of large numbers with small numbers (e.g. for % 7, we repeatedly multiply most-significant digit by 10-7=3 and add it to the next one, mod 7, until there's only a single digit left).

Q: Search text file and count occurrences of a specified string A:

One way to do this would be to loop over the words after you split the line and increment count for each matching word:

user_search_value = input("Enter the value or string to search for: ")

count = 0    

with open(file.txt, 'r') as f:
    for line in f.readlines():
        words = line.lower().split()
        for word in words:
            if word == user_search_value:
                count += 1
print(count)

Q: Why is CMake introducing -std:c++14 instead of /std:c++14 for compiling with MSVC? A:

tl;dr: CMake's behavior is fine; Just add -Zc:__cplusplus as well.

Your problem is not with CMake; it is generating a legitimate flag. You see, the MSVC compiler (cl.exe) accepts switches specified by either dashes (-) or slashes (/). So your compiler is trying to compile your program using the C++14 standard... except that its support is somewhat dodgy. Specifically, MSVC does not define the __cplusplus preprocessor macro, and your code probably tries to check its values and complains, e.g.:

static_assert(__cplusplus >= 201402L, "C++2014 is required to compile this program");

to fix this, you need to pass another command-line option: /Zc:__cplusplus (or alternatively, -Zc:__cplusplus). That will correctly make the definition.

Edit: You may also want to use /Zc:preprocessor for (newer) MSVC's preprocessor to conform to the C and C++ language standards better. See this description.
